title: lore new: the hyphenated slug for the Attested Computation type is unreachable, and silently degrades to unknown-type-warning-only validation
description:
Reported by opum-agent 2026-09-18, measured against the installed 0.7.0 binary. Independently
re-verified here against dev at HEAD, via `bun run src/cli.ts` in a throwaway bundle -- STILL
PRESENT, not already fixed.

THE DEFECT: Attested Computation is the one multi-word built-in type, and it is unreachable from
its own natural slug.

  lore new attested-computation "Probe"

produces `type: attested-computation` (verbatim, uncanonicalized), no `# yaml-language-server:
$schema=` modeline, no `runtime` field, and `lore validate` reports only a WARNING --
`unknown type "attested-computation"; validated on 'type' only` -- at exit 0. Meanwhile:

  lore new "Attested Computation" "Probe"

produces the correct `type: Attested Computation`, the `$schema` modeline, `runtime: TODO`, and
validates clean. Every other built-in resolves case-insensitively from its slug (`adr`->ADR,
`runbook`->Runbook, etc.); Attested Computation is the only multi-word one and the only broken one.

ROOT CAUSE, located and confirmed by reading the code, not just reproducing the symptom:
src/core/schema.ts:241-244, `canonicalType`:

  export function canonicalType(input: string, profile: Profile = defaultProfile()): string {
    const trimmed = input.trim();
    return profile.byLowerName.get(trimmed.toLowerCase()) ?? trimmed;
  }

and src/core/profile.ts:696, where the lookup table is built:

  byLowerName.set(type.name.toLowerCase(), type.name);

`"Attested Computation".toLowerCase()` is `"attested computation"` -- a SPACE, not a hyphen. The
lookup key is built by case-folding alone; it never normalizes a hyphen to a space (or vice versa).
So `"attested-computation".toLowerCase()` is `"attested-computation"`, which is not a key in
`byLowerName`, the lookup misses, and `canonicalType` falls through to its `?? trimmed` branch --
the exact same code path used for a genuine unknown/producer-extension type (this is by design for
an unknown type; it is not by design here, because the type IS known, just unreachable from its own
conventional CLI-friendly spelling).

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A COSMETIC MISS: `lore init` ships `attested-computation.schema.json` into
every bundle unconditionally (confirmed: `init.result.created` lists it on a fresh init), so the
type visibly LOOKS supported. The scaffold then emits a plausible-looking file, and `lore validate`
degrades it to the unknown-type floor (a WARNING, not an error, exit 0) rather than refusing. A user
who types the hyphenated slug -- the form every other multi-word CLI convention in this tool
otherwise trains -- gets no error, no hint, and a document that was never actually schema-checked.
That could persist for months before anyone notices, which is exactly the "fails green" shape this
fleet treats as the most dangerous defect class.

FIX SHAPE, not prescribed: normalize the lookup key (fold both hyphens and spaces to a common
separator, e.g. compare `toLowerCase().replace(/[-\s]+/g, ' ')` on both sides) so `attested-computation`,
`attested computation`, and `Attested Computation` all resolve to the same canonical type. Whoever
takes this should also check whether any OTHER multi-word profile-declared type (a custom
`.lore/profile.toml` `[[types]]` entry with a space in `name`) has the same unreachable-slug problem,
since the bug is in the general lookup, not specific to this one built-in.

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore new attested-computation "Probe" resolves to the canonical type Attested Computation -- same $schema modeline, same runtime field, same clean lore validate result as lore new "Attested Computation" "Probe" produces today.

The fix is in the general lookup (canonicalType / byLowerName), not a special case for this one type, and a test proves a custom profile-declared multi-word type is reachable from its hyphenated slug too.
A regression test covers the failure mode this task found: the hyphenated form must not silently fall through to the unknown-type warn-only path.
bun run lint, typecheck and the test suite pass, and lore check exits 0.

implementationNotes:

This task's root cause (canonicalType folds case but never normalizes hyphen-vs-space; profile.ts builds the lookup key as type.name.toLowerCase(), so the space in "Attested Computation" never matches the hyphen in "attested-computation") is confirmed by reading the code, not just reproducing the symptom.
